prompt_md: A 3 by 3 by 3 block of cheese must be cut into 27 small cubes. You may rearrange and stack the pieces between straight cuts. What's the fewest cuts needed?
prompt_short: Cut a 3x3x3 cheese block into 27 cubes, restacking allowed. Fewest cuts?
hint_md: Think about the little cube in the very middle.
explain_intuition_md: Being allowed to stack pieces makes it feel like you can beat 6 cuts. But the center cube has 6 faces, none of them on the outside of the block, and a straight cut can create at most one face of it. So 6 is the minimum, and 6 cuts work even without stacking.
explain_math_md: Center cube: $6$ hidden faces, at most $1$ made per cut, so $\ge 6$ cuts; $2$ cuts in each direction give exactly $6$.
